title: Where to look for records
lead: Three steps: what you need, which organisation is involved and what to do next. The navigator searches the archive's actual list of fonds, including organisations' former names.
notice: The navigator only tells you where records are kept and where to apply. Applications are not accepted on this site.

work.title: Confirm employment or salary
work.text: A certificate for a pension, benefit or employer.

study.title: Confirm studies, an award or another event
study.text: An archival certificate, a copy of an order or an extract.

family.title: Learn your family history
family.text: Where relatives lived and worked, and where to start.

research.title: Study the history of an organisation or place
research.text: For studies, research or local history.

fund.title: Which organisation is it about?
fund.titleFamily: Where did the person work or study?
fund.label: Name of the organisation, institution or enterprise
fund.hint: One or two words are enough. It can be any name the organisation had over the years.
fund.failed: The catalogue is unavailable right now. Try later or open the list of fonds.
fund.empty: No such organisation was found in the list of fonds. See below for what you can do.

result.title: What to do next
result.found: This organisation's records are listed in fonds No. {number}.
result.noteTitle: Note in the list of fonds
result.yearLabel: In what year did you work or study there?
result.yearHint: Organisations changed their names. In the application it is best to give the name used at that time.
result.nameUnknown: The list has no name for {year}: give the current name and the years in the application.
result.notFoundTitle: No fonds found — that does not mean there are no records
result.notFound: Personnel records may have gone to the city personnel-records branch or to a district branch, and organisations that still exist keep their own. Ask the nearest branch of the archive.

work.a: Apply for an archival certificate through eGov.kz, Government for Citizens or the archive's office.
work.b: Give the organisation's name, your position and the years of work; attach a copy of your employment record book if you have one.
work.c: The certificate is issued free of charge within 11 working days.

study.a: Apply for an archival certificate, copy or extract through eGov.kz, Government for Citizens or the archive's office.
study.b: Give the institution, the years and the event to be confirmed; attach any documents you have.
study.c: The service is free; the time limit is 11 working days.

family.a: Collect what is known: surnames, places, years of life and workplaces of your relatives.
family.b: Check the catalogue for fonds of organisations and village councils of that area — they show which years are covered.
family.c: Inventories and files of open fonds are consulted in the reading room; birth, marriage and death records are issued by the civil registry offices.

research.a: Open the fonds record: the years, volume and history of names help judge what it may contain.
research.b: Look at related materials on the site: exhibitions, collections and the timeline.
research.c: Inventories and files are consulted in the archive's reading room — rules and opening hours are on the site.
